This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection
order dated 22.11.2023 passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Court No.
2/Special Judge S.C./S.T. Act, Kanpur Dehat.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 as well as the learned AGA and perused the entire record.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
In this case, appellant made false promise of marriage with the victim and then took her from the house and committed rape.
She was subjected to torture and later on she was Ramsharan Trivedi @ Rohit Trivedi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113377333/

sentences.text: 1 assaulted by the appellant and his two friends as a result present F.I.R. was lodged by the victim herself.
Further submitted that the victim was major at the time of alleged incident and she was willing and consenting party.

There was affair between both the parties as a result in the year 2019 she went with the appellant with jewellery and cash from her house and entered into marriage in a temple, thereafter, started living as husband and wife at Mati near Jainpur Bambe.

She was subjected to demand of rupee one lac and a plot by the family members of the appellant and then she started living in a pooled house where she was again subjected to torture by the members of the family of the appellant as a result present F.I.R. was lodged.
The victim herself disclosed the facts under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the learned Magistrate which show that she was willing and consensus.
There was no any false promise of marriage and no intercourse was done with her under such promise.
There is no any other material on record to show the complicity of the appellant in the present case.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Appellant is in jail since 27.9.2023, having criminal history of two cases out of which in one, he is on bail and in other he has not been named.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 as well as learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and contended that there was false promise of marriage with the victim and thereafter she was compelled by the appellant and his friends and rape was also committed with her which shows that there was no consent on her part, therefore, he is not entitled for bail and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the statement of the victim u/s 164 Cr.P.C. this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Ramsharan Trivedi @ Rohit Trivedi involved in Case Crime No. 310 of 2023,
under Sections 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, P.S. Akbarpur, District Kanpur Dehat be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.

3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
